tagline.text: Mindanao's northern tip, still home to limestone islands and a hidden lake

location.label: Location
location.text: San Jose, Basilisa & Libjo, Dinagat Islands

image.credit: Sanelyn G. Adarne / CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: An island province off the northeastern tip of Mindanao, 1–2 hours by boat from Surigao City. Island hopping among limestone islets, an emerald lake hidden in the forest, and tide pools where the sea rushes in remain largely untouched by tourism, making this a fit for travelers who love adventure.
Dinagat Islands is an island province at the northeastern tip of Mindanao, across the Surigao Strait. It consists of the main island of Dinagat, stretching about
60km

from north to south, and the smaller islands around it, and has seven municipalities including the capital San Jose, along with Basilisa, Libjo, and Loreto. Originally part of Surigao del Norte, it became an independent province through a plebiscite in
, had its status shaken for a time by a Supreme Court ruling, and was finally confirmed in
— making it one of the youngest provinces in the Philippines.

Along the island's west and south coasts, limestone rock islands rising out of the sea are scattered about, in scenery reminiscent of Palawan. Hidden in the forest is emerald-green Lake Bababu, where seawater and freshwater sit in layers, and there are also blue tide pools where seawater flows in and out through gaps in the rock. The island's soil, rich in iron, nickel, and chromium, is covered in red earth that has drawn mining development, while the same unusual soil supports rare plants such as pitcher plants and endemic animals like the Dinagat bushy-tailed cloud rat, rediscovered in
after decades.
The islands also hold historical significance. On
October 17, 1944

, U.S. Army Ranger units landed on the coast of Loreto, Dinagat, ahead of the Leyte landing operation — recorded as the first time the American flag was raised again on Philippine soil during the Pacific War. Since the

, large numbers of followers of the religious group the Philippine Benevolent Missionaries Association (PBMA) have also settled here, shaping the islands' society and politics, and the capital San Jose has a white castle, Islanders Castle, along with a memorial shrine connected to the group's founding family.

Tourist infrastructure remains modest. There are few upscale resorts or large restaurants, and the typical trip centers on chartering a boat to tour the islands and resting at beach huts. That leaves seas uncrowded by people and scenery still largely untouched, making it a good fit for travelers who have already done Siargao, backpackers seeking undiscovered islands, and anyone who enjoys snorkeling and camping.
A limestone lake reached by a forest walk of about
30–45 minutes
with a guide from the Basilisa coast. Freshwater sits in a layer above seawater below, and its still, emerald-green water has a mysterious quality.
A natural pool ringed by rock on the Libjo coast, glowing turquoise as seawater flows in and out. The water is clearest and best for swimming at high tide.

Charter a boat and weave among the rock islands, stopping at small sand beaches and snorkeling spots. Popular stops include Kisses Island, where two rocks meet as if kissing, and Aga Island, with an abandoned house atop its cliff.
A small cove-shaped beach in Basilisa, its fine white sand and clear water considered one of Dinagat's signature views. It's worth combining with a stop at the nearby Pagkawasan and Duyos beaches.
A clear stretch of sea off the Libjo coast, a snorkeling spot where you can see sea turtles and coral reefs. It's a good place to stop for lunch and rest at a beach hut.
A white castle standing on a hill in the capital, San Jose, that stands out against the island's otherwise modest scenery. Whether it's open and its entrance fee vary, so check locally.
A few beach resorts rent out tent sites. Splitting island hopping over two days and spending a night on a beach that feels like a deserted island is the quintessential Dinagat trip.

Boats are usually chartered in two-day blocks, and the captain adjusts the route and number of stops based on weather and tides. The last boat to Surigao stops running in the afternoon, so it's best to be back in San Jose by early afternoon on the final day.
The direct Manila–Surigao flight has been discontinued since
March 30, 2025
, and Surigao Airport (SUG) now has only Cebgo flights from Cebu (about
1 hour
). From Manila, either fly direct on Philippine Airlines or Cebu Pacific to Butuan Airport (BXU), about
1 hour 40 minutes
for about
one way, then take a bus or van about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
to Surigao City, or route through Cebu into Surigao. From Surigao Airport to the pier is about
10–15 minutes
by tricycle.
Passenger ferries and fast ferries run frequently from early morning to afternoon from Surigao City pier to San Jose, the capital of Dinagat province. The trip takes about
1–2 hours
and costs about

, with a pier terminal fee charged separately. The departure pier differs by shipping company, so check before you buy a ticket. A separate village also named "Dinagat" sits on the north of the island, so be sure you're heading to San Jose, the tourist center.
If you want to start island hopping from Basilisa or Libjo, you can take a boat from Surigao Boulevard pier to Basilisa (around
12 noon
, about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
) or to Libjo (around
11 AM
Monday–Saturday, about
3 hours
). There is about one boat a day and the return boat leaves at dawn, so check the schedule in advance.
An overnight passenger ferry runs from Cebu to Surigao, arriving in the morning after about
8–10 hours
, after which you can transfer straight to a boat for Dinagat. A roll-on/roll-off ferry crossing from Liloan in southern Leyte to Surigao also takes about
3–4 hours
, used by travelers coming overland through the Visayas.
Island-hopping boat charter: about
for 2 days, 4–8 people per boat
Tricycle within San Jose: about
for a short distance
Habal-habal overland to Basilisa or Libjo: about
, depending on distance and negotiation
Using a boat arranged in advance through the tourism council, rather than a driver touting for business at the pier, means fewer disputes over price.
Dinagat has Mindanao's east-coast climate type, with no clearly defined dry season and rain year-round, but
February–June
, with relatively little rain and calm seas, is the best time for island hopping.
April–May
in particular has strong sunshine and the clearest water, making for great photos of the tide pools and limestone islands. Daytime temperatures run around
November–January

, alongside the northeast monsoon (Amihan), brings the heaviest rain, and swells rolling in from the Pacific cancel boat trips on many days. The Surigao Strait area also sits along a frequent typhoon path, so during
October–December

it's essential to check the weather forecast and build about a day of slack into your schedule. Holy Week and summer break bring more local travelers, so it's best to book beach huts and boats in advance.

items.note: Per person, on arrival in San Jose

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
Most accommodation is in the capital, San Jose. Lodges and pensions near the pier and market run about

a night; facilities are simple, but they're convenient for starting island-hopping trips. The Basilisa and Libjo coasts have a few small resorts that rent out beach huts and tent sites, letting you camp overnight partway through your island hopping. Rooms are limited and many places don't take online bookings, so it's best to arrange things in advance through the tourism council or a boat operator.

The islands don't have many restaurants aimed at tourists, so San Jose's public market is the center of the food scene. It's common to buy fish, squid, crab, pork, rice, and fruit at the market in the morning and have your boat operator or a resort cook it, for a modest cooking fee. Being a coastal community, the kinilaw (raw fish tossed with vinegar and ginger), charcoal-grilled fish, and crab simmered in coconut milk are all delicious. Small restaurants around the market are enough for a meal at about
. Bring plenty of drinking water and snacks for island hopping.
San Jose has few ATMs, and they often break down or run out of cash. Withdraw plenty of cash in Surigao City to cover the boat fare and accommodation.

Chartered boat fares are per boat, so the more people in your group, the cheaper it gets per person. Looking for a join tour through the Dinagat tourism council or a travel community is another option.
You must visit Lake Bababu with a local guide, and the forest trail is slippery when wet, so wear trekking sandals or sneakers.
The tide pools and limestone islands look very different depending on the tide. It's best to plan your route order with your boat operator around the tides.
It's best to bring your own snorkel gear, life vest, aqua shoes, and dry bag. There's almost nowhere on the island to rent them.
Cell signal drops out along much of the coast. Save your accommodation's and boat operator's contact numbers in advance, and let your family know your itinerary.
Locals mainly speak Surigaonon and Cebuano. English works, but learning a few simple Cebuano greetings will get you a much warmer welcome.
If combining this with a Siargao trip, the cleanest route is to base yourself in Surigao City, visit Dinagat first, then take the boat on to Siargao.
Lake Bababu is in Barangay Melgar in Basilisa, and is said to have an underwater cave about
long running beneath the lake and connecting to the sea. The location and description of each attraction can be found in the Dinagat Islands province's
official tourism guide

The sea around Dinagat borders the Pacific and weather can change rapidly. When the coast guard restricts departures, all boat services stop, so during typhoon and monsoon season, check the latest sailing notices and weather forecast, and build in buffer days.
Most island-hopping boats are small bangkas. Always wear a life vest, and avoid boats that overload beyond capacity or push ahead on high-wave days.
There are no medical facilities on the remote coasts. Bring basic first-aid supplies and antiseptic, and be careful not to cut yourself on coral or rocks.
Mining areas are interspersed across the islands, and some coasts have red, muddy runoff. It's best not to enter mining sites or private property without permission.
The environmental and tourism fee, attraction entrance fees, and whether Islanders Castle is open change often, so check the latest details at the tourist information office after you arrive.
The islands are home to many protected plants and animals. Digging up plants such as pitcher plants or catching wildlife is prohibited.
A surfing island about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours 30 minutes
from Surigao City by boat, famous for Cloud 9 and island hopping.
A lagoon and cave system on Bucas Grande Island south of Siargao, about
